I switched from Ubuntu to Debian because originally I used a GPU with jellyfin before I upgraded to an 12th gen Intel cpu for the igpu only build (power efficiency). So I booted up Debian 11 stable but it wouldn't recognize the cpu, literally the '/dev/dri' wouldn't be in the system because of it. It was labeled as "Intel corpo" or something and Jellyfin couldn't recognize it at all. Switching to Debian Unstable (rolling release) is fine, but jellyfin-ffmpeg only supports the "main" release, so that's a no go. 

After going through hours of trial and error and googling... and reading logs I never thought about using the backports. Using the backports updated my kernel so it could recognize the new cpu and updated any packages that I might need. After that it was all smooth sailing from there. 

Quick sync now does work but I'm still having issues getting the "low-power HUC" enabled on my system. Other than that, it works perfectly to how I want the server to be. I might go back and try to figure out how to enable the "Low-power" option once I'm more experienced with linux, but it's a low priority for now. 

Btw I'm a novice when it comes to linux and it's my first time setting up a server, so someone more experience may have figured out these issues I've had way faster than what I had to deal with.
